title: RIT Dining Notifications
tagline: A Telegram bot that told me how much I could spend on food each day at RIT
summary: RIT gives you Dining Dollars for the whole semester, but the balance doesn't tell you how much you can actually spend today. So I built a Telegram bot that logged into my account, grabbed my new purchases, and told me my daily and weekly budget.

hero.alt: RIT Dining Notifications cover showing a TigerSpend transaction panel flowing through scrape, save, budget and notify steps to phone alerts
hero.caption: New purchases go in, a daily budget comes out on my phone.

sections.heading: Why I built it
body: I wanted a number that changed as I spent. If I spent less than my target one day, I'd have a little more for the rest of the week, and if I went over, the next day's budget would go down. I didn't want to copy every purchase into a spreadsheet to get that.

sections.heading: How it worked
body: I'd send /refresh to the bot. My Python program then opened a browser with Selenium, logged into RIT (I still had to approve the Duo prompt on my phone), opened my dining statement, and read the new purchases with Beautiful Soup.

It saved them to a small JSON file so it never sent the same alert twice, then messaged me each new purchase and my updated budget. /checkfunds just did the math from the saved file without logging in again.

media.alt: Looping animation of the RIT Notifications Telegram bot showing my name, dining balance, help, budget-check, refresh and Duo-login steps
media.caption: The bot in August 2024. Only the old connection password is blurred.

sections.heading: Talking to Telegram
body: I talked to Telegram's API directly instead of using a library, which made it really clear how a message gets from my phone to my code and back.

media.alt: TigerSpend statement showing transaction dates and dining-location descriptions with financial details excluded
media.caption: The statement the bot read from, with personal details and amounts cut out.

sections.heading: Scrapers break
body: The RIT site has changed since 2024, enough to break a few of the things my code expected, like how dates are written. That's the problem with scrapers: the website changes and your code doesn't. If I rebuilt it, I'd keep my login settings out of the code and add tests with saved pages, so I'd know right away when something breaks.

notes: DATE: 2024-08 is inferred from the first project's Git history (August 24-25, 2024). The currently linked replacement repository begins September 17, 2024; its commit history explains that it replaced an earlier repository after credentials were accidentally committed. SOURCE: inspected the replacement repository and an isolated local worktree. Verified the Selenium/Beautiful Soup statement scraper, JSON transaction storage, Telegram getUpdates/sendMessage calls, connection-code flow, /start, /disconnect, /help, /status, /checkfunds and /refresh commands, plus daily and weekly budget calculations. LIVE VERIFICATION: on September 16, 2026, authenticated to the current TigerSpend site in the user's normal browser, selected Dining Dollars (Rollover), requested a six-month statement, and observed 22 transaction rows. The included TigerSpend recording is that real workflow, cropped and redacted to exclude the user's name, account identifier, balances, amounts, session URL, browser chrome and unrelated desktop content. The original program was not run end-to-end because its separate Selenium session could not reuse the authenticated session and the historical stored login no longer authenticated; no Telegram messages were sent. A compatibility test copy accepted current account links and date formats; Python compilation and focused date parsing tests passed, but those source changes are not represented as shipped project code. TELEGRAM MEDIA: RPReplay_Final1724599957.MP4 was recorded on August 25, 2024 and supplied by the user from Downloads. Reviewed the full 76.7-second recording and retained a concise 14-second sequence showing /start, /help, /checkfunds, /refresh, the Duo prompt, scraper progress, and statement navigation. Audio was removed because it did not convey project information. The page uses that sequence as a silent looping animated WebP, so it starts without requiring the visitor to press play. At the user's direction, his displayed name, historical dining balance, and daily and weekly figures remain visible; only the old four-digit connection password is blurred. SECURITY: secret.py and token values were never copied into this portfolio. The configured bot identity was verified through Telegram getMe without sending a message. DEVELOPMENT: left null pending the user's classification.
